title: 2007 AMC 10A Problem 15
statement: Four circles of radius \(1\) are each tangent to two sides of a square and externally tangent to a circle of radius \(2,\) as shown. What is the area of the square?

solutions.text:
Consider the isosceles right triangle joining the center of the radius-\(2\) circle to the centers of two adjacent small circles. Its legs have length \(2 + 1 = 3,\) so its hypotenuse is \(3\sqrt2.\)

The side of the square exceeds this hypotenuse by \(2\) (one radius on each end), so \(s = 2 + 3\sqrt2.\)

The area is \[ \begin{aligned} (2 + 3\sqrt2)^2 &= 4 + 12\sqrt2 + 18 \\ &= 22 + 12\sqrt2. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Connect the center of the large circle to the centers of two adjacent small circles
